findings.title: What it is
findings.said: A contract with no name on the explorer.

findings.title: How old the contract is
findings.said: It was created 21 days ago, in block 20817840 (the chain has no code at this address one block earlier).

findings.title: Can anyone read the code
findings.said: The source of the code behind this proxy (0xc404…7e0e) is not verified: all anyone can see is bytecode.
findings.why: Unverified code is a black box. You'd be trusting it without anyone being able to check what it does with your tokens.

findings.title: Can its code be swapped
findings.said: Yes, by one private key: it is a proxy running 0xc404…7e0e, and its owner() is a plain wallet, 0x54f8…5ff4.
findings.why: Whoever holds that one key can swap the code at any moment, without asking anyone, including for code that drains what you approved.

findings.title: Has its code been swapped
findings.said: Yes: the code running today was put in 19 hours ago, in block 22622345, 20 days after the contract went live (pharosscan still shows the older 0xafbe…60ac; the chain says 0xc404…7e0e).
findings.why: The contract you'd be trusting changed this week, and nobody can read the new code. Whatever people trusted it for before doesn't carry over.

findings.title: Who has approved it
findings.said: In the last 100000 blocks (about 26 hours), 71 wallets approved it to move their tokens (109 approvals, 109 of them unlimited).
findings.why: Approvals stay open when the code behind them changes. Everything here is reachable by whoever controls this contract.

findings.title: What its owner can do
findings.said: Its bytecode has functions to swap in different code (upgrade).
findings.why: These are normal in many tokens, but each one is a lever someone holds over your money. With unverified code you can't see who may pull it.
